heading: What `realtime` does NOT enforce from `linear_scan: false`
text:
### What `realtime` does NOT enforce from `linear_scan: false` [LNLS.2.4]

The following `linear_scan: false` constraints are **not** required for hard RT
and are **not** automatically enforced by `realtime`:

| LNLS constraint | Why `realtime` does not need it | What it means for T_wcet |
|---|---|---|
| LNLS.3.1 — no JSON slots | Borrow semantics make JSON slot assert O(1). JSON_PATH is already blocked (LNLS.3.9). LIVE blocks re-assertion. JSON slots are RT-compatible. | No impact |
| LNLS.3.3 — logical identity join required | Multi-pattern joins not anchored to logical identity slots fall back to O(L_β × T_j), bounded by N_max — finite, computable, valid hard RT. | T_wcet contains O(N_max × T_j) beta term instead of O(1) |

**Practical implication**: `realtime` alone is sufficient for hard RT as defined by the
realtime contract ([RTCT.1]).  Adding `linear_scan: false` eliminates the O(N_max)
dependency from join costs entirely (beta joins become O(1) via the
logical-identity-slot constraint).
This is a T_wcet improvement, not an RT prerequisite.
